# Philadelphia: age and tenure, 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS

<!-- Generated by analysis/age_tenure/pums_age_tenure.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Source: Census Bureau 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS, the 11 Philadelphia PUMAs (3,298 sampled households, 7,632 sampled persons). Counts are weighted and rounded to the nearest 100; ± is the 90% margin of error from the 80 replicate weights. "Older" means 65 or over. Method and definitions: the script's docstring.

## 5. "Cash poor, house rich" owners

Cash poor = household income below 200% of poverty. House rich = home value at or above the median owner-occupied value in Philadelphia, $240,000.

| Owner households | Cash poor and house rich | Share of group | Share cash poor (any value) | Share owning free and clear |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Householder 65+ | 14,800 ± 2,900 | 12% ± 2 | 37% ± 4 | 65% ± 3 |
| Householder under 65 | 19,500 ± 3,600 | 8% ± 1 | 29% ± 3 | 34% ± 3 |

## 6. Reported property tax as a share of household income

Share of each owner group; TAXAMT is the respondent's reported annual real-estate tax, so it reflects whatever relief the household receives.

| Tax / income | Householder 65+ | Householder under 65 |
|---|---|---|
| Under 2% | 31% ± 4 | 37% ± 3 |
| 2-4% | 24% ± 3 | 30% ± 3 |
| 4-6% | 13% ± 3 | 13% ± 2 |
| 6-10% | 13% ± 2 | 9% ± 2 |
| 10% or more | 16% ± 2 | 9% ± 1 |
| No or negative income | 2% ± 2 | 2% ± 1 |

Median reported tax as a share of reported value: 0.88% (65+), 1.02% (under 65). Both inputs are self-reported and TAXAMT is published as bracket midpoints, so a single household's ratio is noisy; among sampled owners (unweighted) the 10th-90th percentile range of tax/value is 0.31%-2.07%.

Older-owner households paying 6% or more of income in property tax (or with no income): 37,600 ± 4,400.

## 7. Older-renter households (householder 65+)

Gross rent as a share of household income. "Not computed" covers no-cash-rent and zero-income households.

| Rent / income | Households | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Under 30% | 20,100 ± 3,800 | 37% ± 7 |
| 30-49% | 11,600 ± 3,200 | 21% ± 5 |
| 50% or more | 18,600 ± 3,700 | 34% ± 5 |
| Not computed | 4,300 ± 1,900 | 8% ± 3 |

Share of older-renter households below 200% of poverty: 64% ± 6 (older owners: 37% ± 4). People 65+ living in renter households: 65,400 ± 6,400.

## 8. Building type of older households

A household's change under a land-value tax depends on its parcel's land share, which the survey does not measure. Building type is the closest survey proxy: units in large buildings sit on little land per household.

| Units in structure | Older owners | Older renters |
|---|---|---|
| Detached house | 15% ± 2 | 3% ± 2 |
| Rowhouse / twin (attached) | 73% ± 3 | 29% ± 5 |
| 2-4 units | 3% ± 1 | 18% ± 5 |
| 5-19 units | 2% ± 1 | 9% ± 4 |
| 20+ units | 7% ± 2 | 41% ± 6 |
| Mobile home / other | 0% ± 0 | 1% ± 1 |
